her_case.note: One dating (decision 43, adopted 2026-10-01): global_crash's index 0 is the state measured on data to September 2026 (unemployment in August, inflation to August, the policy rate at end-September, the gap at zero): the end of 2026Q3, gc.START. Each index after it is one simulated quarter, and ai_shock's falls begin at index 1 (delay 0), so the bust's first falls are in 2026Q4 and 2028Q4 is index 9. Until 2026-10-01 the labels ran one quarter late, since log 28: case.py's END_2028 = 8 and its header's 'quarter 1 = 2026Q4' (counted from 1) were in place at log 28's commit, and log 29's START = 2026Q4 at index 0 kept them. So her case was already an October bust; case.py, case.json and STATE now carry the measured labels (the values quoted before are in STATE's log). On it her case's pace is half-way in 2028Q2, its tariffs arrive in 2027Q1, its premium builds over 2026Q4-2027Q3, and robotics begins in 2028Q4 and is complete by 2029Q3.

oil_rule.note: the watcher's rule is on daily data; the earlier month-end reading ('clears 2026-10') missed that it comes back on in November (armed) and fires in December under 'stays high' or 'held high'; 'together' (the first wording) and 'level_based_together' (the condition as amended) count weekdays (the bust rules' calendar), with the Brent prints among them beside the first

memory.note: the rule joined the watcher on 25 Sep and fired on its first run; the replay's earlier fires are what it would have done, and the difference in memory does not change any later date

threshold.definition: dated Brent held at L from 30 Sep 2026 through 2027Q3 (the 'stays high' shape: then the geometric midpoint with the three-year average, then the three-year average), the oil rule replayed daily; met = Brent at least 1.25 times its three-year average (level-based: decision 27 as amended 2026-10-01), or the oil rule active (the first wording, superseded), on a day bust.us.equity, bust.credit.us or crash.joint is active, at both ends

futures_strip.source: front-month Brent futures in late September (the reviews' news check; not a series in these sources)

threshold.note: decision 27 as amended (2026-10-01, level-based) needs $101.12 held from 30 Sep, and is met at the futures strip. The first wording (superseded) was a knife-edge: met only if dated Brent holds at $109.65 or more from 30 Sep through late December; 'stays high' ($117.66) is 7.3% above that and the last print ($113.96) 3.9%; at the futures strip ($102-107) the oil rule goes off in mid-October and does not come back on, so the first wording is not met there.
